recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Continue to treat individual Medication Definition tracker items as separate issues; FHIR-31757 itself is best retained as an umbrella audit that the R4B refactor and later issue-specific work already satisfied.
issue_request: Applied/Persuasive BR&R R4 ballot comment for the MedDef grouping. It asked that committees be allowed enough time to fix the R4 Medication Definition resources, noting that the R4 versions were not implementable and that significant refactoring should still be compatible with R4. The recorded resolution says many improvements have been made.
initial_application: No Jira-keyed source commit for FHIR-31757 was found. The broad application appears in Medication Definition history, especially commit e45413f7a7c4825937ad64d7800f54ff8ae3e0f2, which created the Medication Definition module page, removed/refactored the old R4 MedicinalProduct* and substance-definition surfaces, and updated R4B configuration/history. Later issue-specific Medication Definition changes were handled through separate tracker commits and reconciliation commits.
additional_context: Current fhir.ini keeps the Medication Definition resources in build scope, and current history.html documents the R4B rename/collapse/removal set. The Medication Definition module now explains the regulatory/catalog, prescribing-support, and definition-vs-instance boundaries. BR&R/Pharmacy meeting records from the ballot cycle discuss MedDef ballot reconciliation and MPD/MK boundary work. No direct Zulip or Confluence reference for FHIR-31757, and no conflicting later decision, was found.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current spec already reflects the broad approved outcome for this umbrella ballot comment, and adding generic explanatory prose would be redundant rather than a necessary semantic correction.
